I'm looking at atom CE1 in the PHE69 ring and tracing which nearby atoms fall within two bonds—CD1, CZ, CG, and CE2 need to be excluded, while CD2 sits three bonds away and stays in consideration.

Calculating the CE1-CD2 distance gives about 2.78 Å, consistent with their para relationship across the ring. Checking CB confirms it's also three bonds away but farther at 3.78 Å, so now I'm scanning coordinates of nearby residues to see what else falls close to CE1's position.

I'm going through residues LYS60, ARG62, and TYR70, but their coordinates don't line up in y or z with the target region, so I'm now focusing on PHE69's own ring atoms like CD1 to check proximity.

Continuing to scan GLY68, ILE61, LEU64, SER66, and GLY67 for coordinates that might match, but none of their side-chain positions fall within the range I'm searching.

Checking other candidates too -- chain B residues, ARG32, GLU33, TRP5 -- but nothing else lands close enough. It seems like CD2 of PHE69 at 2.778 Å is the intra-residue answer, though I should double check whether the question really wants a distinct heavy atom outside the immediate bonding network rather than one within the same residue.

I keep scanning for anything closer than 2.78 Å, going through LEU64, GLY67, ARG62, ILE61, LYS63, ASP65, and PHE77 -- none of their atoms fall within range.

After checking GLN76, SER73, TYR70, and PHE69's other atoms, nothing beats the intra-residue CD2 distance, so I'm settling on A:F69:CD2 as the closest excluded-bond atom.
